title: Office & admin
_note: English for work (english-for-work run, 2026-11-02): written by hand in British English, not yet checked by a second reader. translations.en = short definition in simple English; deHint = German translation (the 'German' tab). Words that already exist in the English lexicon are refs with a job-specific example.
intro: The words for work in an office: equipment, emails, meetings, keeping data safe and talking to customers and colleagues on the phone. Every word has an example sentence from a real working day in the UK.
introEasy: Do you work in an office? Learn the words for computers, emails, meetings and phone calls here.
tipps: In emails, start with “Dear Ms Khan” or “Hi Tom” and end with “Kind regards”. Keep the sentences short and put the question or request near the top.
On the phone, speak slowly and spell names and numbers: “That's K-A-H-N.” It is fine to say “Could you repeat that, please?”
British colleagues often soften requests: “Would you mind sending me the file?” sounds friendlier than “Send me the file.”
